div.div: Parsing and windowing turn free text into a count matrix: every column is a template an engineer can read, and the order of events inside a window is lost

raw line (logcat threadtime layout)
date time pid tid level tag: message
... 812 845 I wpa_supplicant: CTRL-EVENT-DISCONNECTED bssid=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff reason=3 locally_generated=1

template = constant words, parameters replaced by <*>
CTRL-EVENT-DISCONNECTED bssid=<*> reason=<*> locally_generated=<*>
-> one stable template ID (a vocabulary of a few hundred, e.g. 400 templates [1*])

parameters = the run-time values, kept
[aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, 3, 1]
reason 3 [2] = deauthenticated because leaving (IEEE 802.11); parameters often name the cause [B5]
B. Match it fast: a parse-tree matcher over a fixed template set [B1]

one layer per token
partial-token wildcards keep event=<*> and error=<*> apart
no template matches -> unmatched bucket: engineers review, add templates, rebuild the tree [C2]

Where templates come from [B1]
- mining (Drain, Spell) finds only what is in the sample. Example: a component with 100 print statements [3*], about 50 % [4*] on error or warning paths; a miner on normal logs finds 20 templates [5*]. The missing ones are the error paths detection needs.
- source-code extraction: complete, but needs source access and upkeep.
- Drain speed: 51.85–81.47 % [6] faster than the best online parser of its time, on 5 data sets [7] with more than 10 000 000 log messages [8].
C. Cut the parsed stream into windows [B2]
a device-day of 24 h [9*], window 1 h, step 0.25 h -> 93 windows (my arithmetic; overlapping rows are not independent)
session = one execution path, needs an ID (HDFS block IDs; device logs rarely have one). Public defaults (BGL): fixed 1 h [10], sliding 6 h [11] with step 1 h.
D. Count templates per window: the event count matrix [B2]
toy counts, not data. w3 has unusual counts (red): the kind of row an isolation forest isolates fast [B3].

order is lost
w4 = T1 T2 T3
w5 = T1 T3 T2
same vector [1, 1, 1, 0, 0]
an order fault is invisible to counts -> transition edges [B5]

Window length is a design choice [B2]: longer -> denser vector, frequency changes easier to see, but a short burst is diluted and the earliest alarm is later. Shorter -> faster, better time localisation, but mostly zeros and normal jitter looks large. Set it from the fault classes you care about.

Legend — grey = raw text; green = templates / template columns; amber = parameters, sliding windows and design choices; blue = index layers, fixed windows and window rows; red dashed = where information is lost or left unmatched.

Sources — every number is loaded from ../constants.json. [n] = public (real value, cited); [n*] = illustrative (an invented round number of realistic order of magnitude; never a measurement).
[1*] templates_per_component_set = 400 templates — illustrative; ('a few hundred')
[2] ieee80211_reason_deauth_leaving = 3 reason code — public; IEEE Std 802.11 reason-code table; wpa_supplicant ieee802_11_defs.h (WLAN_REASON_DEAUTH_LEAVING)
[3*] component_print_statements = 100 print statements — illustrative
[4*] component_error_warning_share = 50 % of print statements — illustrative; ('about half')
[5*] miner_templates_found = 20 templates — illustrative
[6] drain_runtime_improvement = 51.85–81.47 % — public; He, Zhu, Zheng, Lyu, 'Drain', ICWS 2017, abstract (vs best online parser of its time)
[7] drain_eval_datasets = 5 data sets — public; He, Zhu, Zheng, Lyu, 'Drain', ICWS 2017, abstract
[8] drain_eval_messages_min = 10 000 000 log messages — public; He, Zhu, Zheng, Lyu, 'Drain', ICWS 2017, abstract ('more than 10 million')
[9*] window_example = day 24, window 1, step 0.25, windows 93 h / count — illustrative; inputs; windows = (24-1)/0.25 + 1, my arithmetic
[10] he2016_fixed_window_default = 1 h — public; He, Zhu, He, Lyu, 'Experience Report: System Log Analysis for Anomaly Detection', ISSRE 2016, §IV-B
[11] he2016_sliding_window_default = window 6, step 1 h — public; He, Zhu, He, Lyu, 'Experience Report: System Log Analysis for Anomaly Detection', ISSRE 2016, §IV-B
